full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman J. This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 07.05.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.10268 of 2007 making the Rule absolute and declaring the Memo No. ওঃপ্রঃ/গুঃশা৩/৪৫২(৩) dated 01.10.2007 in respect of the respondent No.1 herein as writ petitioner's property of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate bearing E.C. No.1690 is illegal, without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. Facts leading, to filing of this civil appeal, is abort, are that the writ petitioner filed the Writ Petition No.IO268 of 2007 before the High Court Division challenging the order dated 30.09.2007 passed under the signature of the writ respondent No.2 contained in Memo No. ওঃপ্রঃ/গুঃশা৩/৪৫২(৩) dated 01.10.2007 in respect of the property-Waqf Estate being E.C. No.1690 stating that the writ petitioner was the Mutwalli of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate being E. C. No.1690 and this Waqf was created by the Waqfnama executed by Azizur Rahman and the same was enrolled in the Office of the respondent No.l. The Waqf deed No. 5303 was executed on 22.03.1928 and since then the properties mentioned in the schedule of the Waqf deed is managed, possessed and controlled by Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate. There is another Waqf Estate in the locality known as Abdaul Gani Waqf Estate and the deed was executed on 22.03.1928 bearing deed No.1402 and its E.C. No.2059. On 18.5.2006, the respondent No.3 filed an application to respondent No.1 praying for exclusion of the property of schedule No.1 of Waqf Deed No.5303 being E.C. No.1690 of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate and for inclusion of the same property in the Waqf deed No.1402 of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate being E.C. No.2059 in the schedule 11 of that Waqf Estate. Then the respondent No.1 through his Inspector of Chattogram Office issued a memo, dated 12.07.2006 directing the Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate to attend the Office of the Inspector of Chattogram and direction also was given to the writ petitioner to attend on 25.07.2006. Accordingly, the writ petitioner attended the Inspector's Office and also took part in the proceeding. The inquiry was held by the Inspector of Chattogram Office as per direction of the writ respondent No.1 under Memo dated 04.07.2006. Upon receiving the report of the Inspector, hearing was held in the Office of writ respondent No. 1. The writ petitioner produced the necessary documents and also submitted written arguments in support of his case. After hearing of the parties, the writ respondent No.2 in a lengthy order dated 30.09.2007 passed order for correction of schedule of Waqf document and the property in question was ordered to be treated as property of Waqf Estate bearing E.C. No. 2059. This order was passed by the writ respondent No.2 under section 49 of the Waqf Ordinance. Therefore, challenging the said order, the writ petitioner finding no other alternative efficacious remedy moved the above mentioned writ petition before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule Nisi. 

 6. Mr. M.I. Farooqi, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant has submitted that, the High Court Division wrongly considered that, section 49 of the Waqf Ordinance, empowered the Administrator of Waqfs to correct the register inasmuch as the High Court Division failed to consider that Rahimun Nessa, Mutawalli and the wife of the Waqif filed Title Suit No.53 of 1945 in the Court of the learned Munsif, praying for declaration of title and the suit was decreed on 31.07.1946, declaring the title of the Abdul Gani Waqf Estate in the suit land and the decree having not been varied or altered and the title having been declared, and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is not maintainable in the eye of law. He has further submitted that, the findings of the High Court Division that "it appears from Annexure-A to the writ petition that there are two deeds bearing Nos.5303 and 1402 respectively. Both of the deeds are registered deeds and the schedule mentioned in one deed cannot be transferred by order of any authority without resolving the ownership by a competent civil court. After determining the fact that the property belonged to a particular individual then the civil court may direct in accordance with law. Since the deeds are registered, in respect of the property mentioned in one schedule cannot be treated in another schedule of the deeds is not based upon the proper assessment of the materials on record inasmuch as the. High Court Division failed to consider that earlier Rahimun Nessa, Mutawalli and the wife of Waqif Abdul Gani filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1945 before the learned Munsif, which was decreed and the title of the Abdul Gani Waqf Estate was declared in the suit property and, thus, the High Court Division committed error resulting in an error in decision in making the Rule absolute and, thereby, occasioned miscarriage of justice and the same is liable to be set aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed. 

 7. Per contra, Mr. Probir Neogi, the learned senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No.1 made sub-missions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He has submitted that, the Waqif Azizur Rahman of Waqf Deed No.5303 registered on 15.11.1928 (E.C. 1690 of 1935) was also the Executive Mutawalli (Mutawalli No.2) of Waqf Deed No.1402, registered on 22.03.1928, (E.C. 2059 of 1937), therein the Waqif Abdul Gani admitted and it is apparent on the face of ; the Deed itself and both the Waqifs had knowledge about the same and there was no conflict or inconsistency in between both the Waqf Deeds as Abdul Gani had rent receiving interest on schedule 11 whereas Azizur Rahman was the tenant and became tenant by registered Kabuliat dated 20.07.1917 and 13.05.1926 of the same schedule as evident from R.S. Khatian Nos. Nos.1236, 1237, 1238 and 1239, and, that position having been maintained, and, valid till coming into operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 by which the rent receiving interest of Taluk by Abdul Gani or his Waqf had stood acquired in the name of the Government and, hence, the land of the Waqf Deed No.1402 dated 22.03.1928 in particular schedule 11 in which Waqif Abdul Gani had rent receiving interest had ; acquired and ceased from the schedule of the said Deed by operation of law. He has further submitted that, Waqif Azizur Rahman acquired title over the schedule' properties of Deed No.5303 from Abdul Gani vide Patta Deed No.3402 dated 12.04.1915, Rent Receipt vide Deed No.730 dated 11.09.1915, Patta Deed No.271 dated 14.01.1919 and 1209 Kabuliat Deed No.272 dated 15.01.1919 and 1210 Sale Deed No. 276 dated 15.01.1919, Rent  বঙ্গদেশের প্রজাস্বত্ব বিষয়ক ১৮৮৫ সালের ৮ আইন নবরহম ‘রায়তি খাস দখলীয় স্বত্ব’ which he continued till coming into operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, and, hence, there-after, the Waqf properties of Deed No.5303 having four schedules retained as it was and being reflected in 1.S. Khatian Nos.187, 187/1, P.S. Dag Nos.506, 508, 509, 510, 511, 512, 513, 514, 515, 680, 681, 682, 683, 684, 685, 1006, 1007 and 1008 corresponding to B.S. Khatian Nos.2937, 683, 2283 and 2935 B.S. Dag Nos.17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 101, 112, 115, 116, 117, 118, 120, 121, 122, 124, 126, 127, 128, 129, 130, 131, 132, 133, 134, 135, 136, 137, 138, 139, 140, 141, 142, 146, 203, 322, 323, 324,360 either in the name of Waqf of Azizur Rahman being Mutawalli on behalf of Fela Gazi Mosque or in the name of other acquiring title from it by registered Sale Deed and all are paying land Development Tax till date. On the contrary no record of rights in favour of the Waqf of E.C. 2059 after acquisition of rent receiving interest by operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and, therefore, the Waqf Administrator have no jurisdiction under section 49 of the Waqf Ordinance to declare title in favour of Waqf Deed No.1402 by deleting the properties from Waqf Deed No.5303 dated 30.09.2007 after 79 years. He has finally submitted that, Title Suit No.53 of 1945 filed by the predecessor of the appellant, the then Mutawalli Rahimunnessa of E.C. No.2059 made Azizur Rahman, the then Mutawalli of E.C. No. 1690 as proforma defendant No.5 wherein she admitted the Waqf Deed and its E.C. No.1690 and Azizur Rahman as tenant (খাস দখলীয় রায়ত স্তিতিবান) praying for decree of Taluka title though her tenant (কায়েমী প্রজা) the defendant No.5, wherein, she got decree on 31.07.1946 heard and disposed of analogous with Rent Suit No.72 of 1945, wherein, both Azizur Rahman and Rahimunnessa as defendant Nos.1 and 2 respectively and, as such, the High Court Division was correct in holding that the respondent No.2, the Administrator of Waqfs who was respondent No.1, in writ petition "fallen in misconception of law and passed the impugned order on finding of law that "since the deeds are registered on, in respect of the property maintained in one schedule cannot be treated in another schedule of the deeds and, as such, the High court Division rightly passed the impugned judgment and order. Hence, therefore, he prays for dismissal the instant appeal. 

 8. Mr. Mostafa Newaz Mohammad, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on 1 behalf of the respondent No.4 made sub-missions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He has submitted that, the findings in Title Suit No.53 of 1945 was that plaintiff Rahimunnessa Mutawalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate had Taluka interest in the suit property and Azizur Rahman who was defendant No.5 in Title Suit No.53 of 1945 was a tenant under Rahimunnessa and rent receiving interests of Rahimunnessa was acquired on passing of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the property was sold on taking permission from the Administrator of Waqf on 13.05.1964, as such, presently, there is no scope to treat the property as the property of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate, (E.C. No.2059) avoiding all the registered documents of title. He has further submitted that, the added respondent No.4 is the owner and possessor about 7 (seven) Gondas of land of the disputed property, where, he is living with his family members by constructing building and on payment of all taxes and dues, vide registered deeds from his predecessor in Interest vendors who got the same from the second Mutawalli Shonajan Bibi of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate on taking sale permission from the Administrator of Waqf on 13.05.1964. He has finally submitted that, in the facts and circumstances of the case, application under section 49 of the Waqf Ordinance is not applicable, which was overlooked by the writ respondent No.3, and, as such, the High Court Division rightly passed the impugned judgment and order. Hence, therefore, he prays for dismissal the instant appeal. 

 'I. Because the High Court Division committed wrong in not considering that section 49 of the Waqf Ordinance, empowered the Administration of Waqfs to correct the register inasmuch as the High Court Division failed to consider that Rahimun Nessa, Mutwalli and the wife of the Nagif filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1945 in the Court of the learned Munsif, praying for declaration of title and the suit was deckeed on 31.07.1946, declaring the title of the Abdul Gani Waqf Estate in the suit land and the decree having not been varied or altered and the title having been declared, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is not maintainable in law and liable to be set aside. 

 II. Because the findings of the High Court Division that “it appears from Annexure-A to the writ petition that there are two deeds bearing Nos. 5303 and 1402 respectively. Both the deeds are registered deeds and the schedule mentioned in one deed cannot be transferred by order of any authority without resolving the ownership by a competent civil court. After determining the fact that the property belonged to a particular individual then the civil court may direct in accordance with law. Since the deeds are registered one, in respect of the property mentioned in one schedule cannot be treated in another schedule of the deeds ........” is not based upon the proper assessment of the materials on record in as much as the High Court Division failed to consider that earlier Rahimun Nessa, Mutwalli and the wife of waqif Abdul Gani filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1945 before the learned Munsif, which was decreed and the title of the Abdul Gani Waqf Estate was declared in the suit property and thus resulted in an error in the decision in making the Rule absolute and thereby occasioned miscarriage of justice.” 

 15. The origin of Waqf can be traced to the impulse of Muslims to do charitable deeds i.e., to endow property ‘in the way of the Almighty Allah’. According to Section 2(1) of the Mussalman Waqf Validating Act, 1913 “Waqf’ means the permanent dedication by a person professing the Mussalman faith of any property for any purpose recognized by the Mussalman Law as religious, pious or charitable. According to section 6(10)of the Bengal Waaf Act, 1934 “Wagqf’ means the permanent dedication by a person professing Islam of any movable or immovable property for any purpose recognized by the Islamic Law as pious, religious or charitable and includes a Waqf of by user. 

 18. From the recital of Waqf deed it appears that the object, for which the property in question has been dedicated, is charitable, pious or religious in nature and a portion of the usufructs should be used by the descendents. Therefore, the dedication was complete and it could not be divested for any other purposes. Therefore, when a property can be used only for religious or charitable purpose, it acquires a permanent character. The Waqf property vests in the implied ownership of the Almighty in the sense that nobody can claim ownership of it. Even in Wagqf al aulad, the property is dedicated to the Almighty and only the usufructs are used by the descendents. Once the property is given to Waqf, it remains for the Waqf forever. The property cannot be alienated or transferred nor is it subject to the rights of inheritance. It cannot be sold or given away to anybody except in accordance with law. The Islamic Law is a sacred Law, and, thus transaction, or obligation is measured by the standards of religious and moral rules. Those rules are developed through analogical reasoning by Muslim Jurists. When ownership of the Waqf property is relinquished by the Waqfi it cannot be acquired by any other person, rather, it is arrested or detained. In Section 56 of the Bangladesh Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 Mutawalli’s power of alienation of Waqf property has been restricted like section 53 of the Bengal Waqf Act, 1934, where the bar to transfer of immovable property of a Waqf was provided. 

 21. In addition concerning the title etc of the case property the High Court Division botched to consider that Rahimun. Nessa wife of the Waqif Abdul Gani as Mutwalli filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1945 in the Court of the learned Munsif, prayed for declaration of Title over the case land which was decreed on 31.07.1946, declaring the title of the Abdul Gani Waqf Estate in the suit land. That means that the findings of the High Court Division that “it appears from Annexure-A to the Writ petition that, there are two deeds bearing Nos. 5303 and 1402 respectively. Both the deeds are registered and the scheduled mentioned in one deed cannot be transferred by the order of any authority without resolving the ownership by a competent Civil Court. After determining the fact that the property belonged to a particular individual then the civil court may direct in accordance with law. Since the deeds are registered one, in respect of the property mentioned in one schedule cannot be treated in another schedule of the deeds......” is not based upon the proper assessment of the materials on record. 

 22. It is depicted from the Waqf deed, namely Abdul Gani Waqf Estate and Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate that deed of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate was written and executed earlier than that of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate, and, Azizur Rahman himself was the comutawalli and witness of earlier deed. So, the property described in the schedule of the deed of Abdul Gaul Waqf Estate, was clearly known to the Azizur Rahman, who made the Waqf deed later on namely in the name of Azimur Rahman Waqdf Estate. Since the Azizur Rahman admittedly co-mutawalli /2nd mutawalli and witness of the earlier deed. It is absurd and cannot gift some of the plots of earlier Waqf deed to his later waqf deed. Moreso, earlier in Title Suit No.53 of 1945 filed by the Mutawalli of Rahimunnessa Waqf Estate against the tenant for declaration and realization of land, wherein, it has been declared that, the disputed plots are belonged to Abdul Gani Waqf Estate as per Waqf Deed. Therefore, later on, inserting the same plot to the Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate deed is not valid and according to the provision of Registration Act prior registered deed will prevail over the later registered deed. 

 23. In the earlier title suit, Azizur Rahman was the proforma defendant No.5, and, contested against the principal defendant- tenant along with the plaintiff- Rahimunnesa for evicting tenant. In that decree, it was also decided that, the Azizur Rahman was the tenant under the Rahimunnessa, the Mutawalli of Abdul Gani Waaf Estate. Therefore, the question is whether while the Tenancy Act has come into being the tenant becomes the owner of the property. Therefore, the Waqf Estate cannot claim the right, title and ownership in that property. 

 24. We have given our anxious consideration to the above contentions, it appears to us that, the suit property was declared, property of Waqf Estate before enactment of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and, it cannot be denied that, by the parties that, while suit property is the property of Waaf Estate, it cannot be later on, by dint of State Acquisition and Acquisition Tenancy Act, the property of a tenant. Because, the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act itself has given legal entitlement by enacting provision of section 20(5)(i)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 which runs as follows: 

 (ii) Where, under any debutter, waqf- al-al-aulad or any other trust, the income from the lands covered by such trust is partly dedicated for religious or charitable purposes and partly reserved for the pecuniary benefit of any individual, only portion of the lands, as may be selected in accordance with the rules to be made in this behalf by the Government shall come within the purview of sub-clause (c)  of clause (1). 

 27. In view of such law, it is apparent on the face of the record, that by dint of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the tenant of Waqf Estate cannot claim the ownership of a property as a tenant. 

 28. Moreso, there is a legal bar to transfer of immovable property of a Waaf Estate by any of mutawalli under sections 56(1)(2)(3)(4) and (5) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 (Ordinance No. 1 of 1962). It runs as follows: 

 17[57A.(1) Notwithstanding anything contained to the contrary in the Registration Act, 1908 (Act No. XVI of 1908), no Sub-Registrar shall register any deed of transfer of any immovable property belonging to a waqf, without the previous sanction of the Administrator or the Government, as the case may be. (2) If a Sub-Registrar, knowingly and intentionally, registers a deed in violation of the prohibition under sub-section (1), he shall be liable for commission of the offence of abetment of criminal breach of trust.”
